title: The water before the words
told: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? do you have a small thing you do to switch from one part of your day to the next?
options: then you already get half of this one. listen.
then this story might hand you one. listen.
that’s okay. this one is about the smallest habit there is.

steps.line: In Medina lived a man named Bilal. He had once been enslaved. Freed, he became the one who called people to prayer, his voice carrying over the roofs at dawn.
One morning after the dawn prayer, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ turned to him: “Bilal, I heard your footsteps ahead of me in paradise. What have you been doing?”

steps.q: What do you think Bilal’s secret was?
o: He gave away all he had
He kept up one small habit
steps.why: One small habit. The Prophet ﷺ asked because he’d heard Bilal’s footsteps, not because of any big deed people had seen.

steps.line: Bilal answered, “The deed I hope in most is this: whenever I make wudu, by day or by night, I pray with it.” Wudu is the washing before prayer.

steps.q: Bilal prayed after every wudu, even when no prayer was due. What would that prayer be?
o: Two short units of extra prayer
A full set of the five prayers
A long prayer through the night
steps.why: Two short rak‘ahs. Many Muslims still pray them after wudu, a habit traced to Bilal: a minute or two, kept every time.

steps.line: The washing itself comes from one verse of the Qur’an: wash the face, and the arms up to the elbows, wipe the head, then the feet.
And a saying of the Prophet ﷺ pictures it: as the water runs off the face, the hands and the feet, the wrongs they did run off with it.

steps.q: People often make wudu when their hands are already clean. So why picture wrongs running off with the water?
o: A health rule, like washing before meals
It washes the heart, not just the hands
Water was scarce, so it had to count
steps.why: Wudu isn’t really about dirt. It lets the day run off, so you step into the prayer new.

steps.line: Today, at a row of taps by a mosque door, or at an ordinary kitchen sink, Muslims still stop for the water before the prayer.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Someone is traveling with no water, and it’s time to pray. What does the same verse allow?
o: They wait until they reach water
They wipe with clean earth instead
steps.why: It’s called tayammum: you touch clean earth and wipe the face and hands. The Qur’an gives it in the same verse as wudu (5:6), so no one is shut out of prayer.

say: here’s what i love. bilal’s secret wasn’t grand. he washed, and then he prayed. every time.
in islam, wudu is the step between the street and the prayer. the water readies you inside and out, every single time.

steps.q: Bilal didn’t name a great fast or a great gift. Why might his footsteps still have been heard in paradise?
o: He washed more often than anyone
His voice called all of Medina
Small deeds kept up are dear to God
steps.why: Not a grand deed: a small one, kept up every time. The Prophet ﷺ said the deeds God loves most are the steady ones, even if small.

today.say: learn the order of wudu from the verse today: face, arms to the elbows, a wipe over the head, then the feet. those are the steps the verse names; a teacher can show you the whole of wudu, which begins with the hands, mouth and nose. it’s your choice: just learn it, watch someone make wudu, or try it yourself, slowly.
options: lovely. face, arms, head, feet. that’s the whole verse in four steps.
beautiful. one slow wash, then a quiet moment. that’s how bilal’s small habit went.

card.from: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ
card.keepWhy: Muslims wash before they pray, like Bilal.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1149; Sahih Muslim 2458 (Bilal’s footsteps in paradise, asked after the dawn prayer; he prays after every purification)
Qur’an 5:6 (face, arms to the elbows, head, feet), paraphrased
Sahih Muslim 244 (the wrongs leave with the water)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6464; Sahih Muslim 783 (the most beloved deeds to God are the most regular, even if few)
Bilal as the caller to prayer: Sunan Abi Dawud 499 (the dream of the adhan; “teach it to Bilal, for his voice is stronger”)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3754 (Bilal freed by Abu Bakr: “Abu Bakr is our master, and he freed our master”)
check: Caption 3 shortens Bukhari 1149 (“I have done no deed I hope in more than that whenever I purify myself, by day or night, I pray with it what was written for me”). Confirm.
“Then the feet” is kept neutral on the Sunni and Shia difference (washed or wiped), as in the day-3 script. Confirm.
